Hi Liam,

Thanks — we can absolutely map your Q3–Q4 forecast into a reservation recommendation. I created a compact workbook that does three things:
- Maps forecasted token/embedding volume into equivalent GPU-hour demand per month using your mix of short chat sessions and large-batch embeddings.
- Shows candidate GPU blends (A100-80GB, H100-80GB, and an LLM-optimized T4/RTX blend for lower-cost async jobs) with per-GPU throughput at your 95th P99-ish latency target (we used 75ms target per your note).
- Computes the commitment gap between your expected sustained baseline and the reservation tiers we offer, plus an estimated burst delta and recommended burst pool sizing.

I attached: ariadne_rfi_workbook_v1.xlsx (the mapping workbook), a short playbook PDF (redwood_gpu_blend_playbook.pdf) with the assumptions and kernel-fit notes, and a CSV summary (commitment-gap-summary.csv). Key callouts in the workbook:

1) Baseline vs burst: For your forecasted peak month (Sept), baseline sustained token rate maps to ~120 A100-equivalent GPU-hours/day. Reserving a 1:1 A100 pool for baseline would require ~40 A100 GPUs committed (monthly commit). However, because a portion of your job mix is latency-tolerant batch embedding (30% of tokens in our model), we recommend a hybrid: 28 A100-80GB (low-latency chat) + 6 H100-80GB (throughput-critical inference), plus a 10-node burst lane that can be auto-borrowed at 2x throughput for short windows.

2) Cost and quantization sensitivity: If you accept 4-bit quantized FP16 paths for embeddings, you can drop the recommended committed H100 count by ~25% with a small quality tradeoff we call out in the playbook.

3) Risk and SLA: We included a fallback plan that routes traffic to the hosted pool (with higher cost and slightly higher tail latency) when burst lane consumption exceeds 60% for more than 15 minutes. This keeps critical flows alive during unexpected spikes.

Can priyom and marcus review the workbook for any technical caveats? Liam — if this looks reasonable I can schedule a 30-min walkthrough Wed morning (May 7) to finalize the commitment mix and a proposed term sheet.

Best,

Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0192

Vanessa — quick technical review notes after checking the workbook against Ariadne's forecast: 

- The spreadsheet assumes a median sequence length of 64 tokens for chat and 1,600 tokens for batch embeddings; Ariadne's original forecast shows an embedding job mix skewed toward 3k tokens for some customers. If that holds, the H100 hours will increase ~18%. I've added a 'long-embed' adjustment tab in the workbook (tab: long_embed_adj).
- Suggest swapping 2 of the proposed H100s for A100-80GB with an optimized kernel path for your chat models — this improves tail latency for mixed workloads where KV cache locality matters. Marcus, I'm flagging the kernel-fit note for you to check optimizer compatibility.
- Burst sizing: instead of a static 10-node burst lane, recommend an adaptive burst policy that scales by request family (chat vs batch) and enforces the 15-minute guardrail Vanessa mentioned. This will reduce over-provisioning in steady high-variance months.

I'll update the workbook and re-export the summary later today. Vanessa — please push the latest files and I'll confirm the numbers for the term sheet.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
